title: Musk’s Terafab to Spend Over $100 Billion for First In House AI Chips

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Terafab will require tens of billions of dollars in capital equipment by early 2028 to launch its chip manufacturing operations, Elon Musk said. The joint venture between Tesla and SpaceX faces total long-term costs that will likely exceed $100 billion, though the specific funding split between the two companies remains undecided. Most equipment orders for the first fabrication plant are already placed as the company pushes to vertically integrate its AI hardware production.

ASML and other machinery providers have expedited shipments to support an "insanely fast" timeline that targets a functional SRAM test chip by May or June 2027 at a research facility in Austin. Volume production is aimed for the third or fourth quarter of 2028 at the primary Gibbons Creek site in Texas. To accelerate the project, SpaceX is utilizing its rocket-engine casting capabilities to produce turbine components, which Musk claims will bring electrical power online up to 18 months faster than traditional methods.

selectedTweets.bestBit: volume production around Q3'28, and credits ASML for “accelerating equipment deliveries”
selectedTweets.text:
Elon Musk reveals chip-fab "breakthroughs" he won’t discuss on the earnings call, says TeraFab’s first test chip is due around May or June next year with volume production around Q3'28, and credits ASML for “accelerating equipment deliveries”

“Well, I mean, we’re just figuring out chip fabrication. So, but I’ll tell you what our internal expectations are, which obviously I put, you know, big error bars in this because we don’t know if we will actually achieve this or not, but it’s what we’re aiming for internally: is to make our first sort of test chip functional in approximately May or June of next year."

"That’s just kind of a SRAM chip or something to basically test the line. That’s at the Research Fab in Austin."

"And we’re aiming to, our aspiration is to reach volume production around Q3 of ‘28 at TeraFab, at Gibbons Creek, the main TeraFab location. These were very aggressive dates, and we’re very appreciative of ASML and all of our other suppliers in accelerating equipment deliveries in order to achieve this outcome."

"Let’s just say that that outcome of achieving volume production is at least in the set of possible outcomes for Q3 or Q4 of ‘28. So these are obviously like insanely fast timeframes for chip production."

"We do have, I think, some significant potential breakthroughs in chip fabrication, but I don’t think I should discuss that on earnings call.”

"Let’s not give away the shop here. But I am optimistic that we will dramatically accelerate chip production and that TeraFab will ultimately do what the name suggests, which is to make a terawatt of superintelligence chips per year.”

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
According to Korean media, Elon Musk's Terafab is now talking to almost EVERY Korean chip supplier it can find.

Until now, the only known Korean suppliers were HPSP and Hanmi Semiconductor.

Now TheElec reports that Tesla and SpaceX are in talks across nearly every category Korean companies can supply, from basic piping parts to process materials to test components.

At SEMICON West in San Francisco last week, Terafab staff walked straight to around 10 Korean booths on the morning of day one, including ENF Technology, Dongjin Semichem, Hanmi Semiconductor, Unisem and MiCo.

Several companies have already signed NDAs. One got an NDA by email the same evening Terafab visited its booth.

Hanmi Semiconductor is discussing TC bonders for Terafab, and HPSP has agreed to supply one high pressure hydrogen annealing tool to the R&D line.

MiCo's cleaning unit Komico signed a three way NDA with Tesla and SpaceX about a month ago, and ISC is already swapping samples for rubber test sockets.

Tesla and SpaceX do not buy from Chinese suppliers. One Korean supplier put it simply, without China there are only a few options, and Japan is expensive.

They also want prices that are CHEAPER than China.

$LRCX and $AMAT have reportedly built dedicated Terafab teams, and Fujifilm is meeting Terafab buyers regularly on slurries, photoresist and etchants.

The goal is a fab with 1 million wafer starts per month within 10 years, with $16.8 billion of initial investment and more than 3,000 jobs.

SpaceX broke ground in Grimes County, Texas this month, and the first 100,000 wafer per month phase is expected before 2030.

Logic is being done with $INTC, talks with $TSM are ongoing, and memory will be built separately.

One supplier said that if they email Terafab in the middle of the night in the United States, they get an answer in 30 minutes to an hour.

$TSLA and $SPCX are building a chip supply chain at Elon speed.

selectedTweets.bestBit: SpaceX is using its rocket-engine casting shop to make turbine blades and vanes... so it can bring power online 12 to 18 months faster than anyone else
selectedTweets.text:
Elon Musk says SpaceX is using its rocket-engine casting shop to make turbine blades and vanes, the parts that run 12 to 18 months behind the rest of the turbine, so it can bring power online 12 to 18 months faster than anyone else

“So we’re casting the blades and vanes for the turbines. So SpaceX already has a very advanced castings capability that was developed for rocket engines."

"So we have, I think, actually the most advanced casting capability on Earth, because the demands for castings for rocket engines exceed the demands for anything else you could possibly imagine."

"So, taking that incredible team that has, I think, objectively the most advanced casting technology in the world and saying, hey, can you guys also make some blades and vanes for terrestrial turbines is much easier than what they have done in the past."

"And when we talk to the turbine suppliers, they tell us that the blades and vanes are 12 to 18 months behind the rest of the turbine. Meaning they can deliver everything except the blades and vanes 12 to 18 months before they can deliver the blades and vanes."

"So casting is this really difficult bottleneck. And if anything, it seems to be getting worse."

"So that means that we can bring power online 12 to 18 months faster than anyone else."

"That’s the kind of advantage that’s difficult to replicate. Unless someone else is building an advanced casting shop, they will be unable to compete with SpaceX in this regard.”

selectedTweets.text:
Exclusive reporting by Korean media on Terafab:

Terafab is excluding Chinese suppliers entirely. It wants to work with Korean suppliers because Japanese products are expensive. However, it is asking Korean companies to offer prices even lower than those of Chinese suppliers.

Terafab decided in advance which companies to approach and which products to discuss at SEMICON West 2026, then visited their booths as soon as the show opened.

Leading global semiconductor equipment suppliers Lam Research and Applied Materials have set up dedicated Terafab teams.

The initial facility, with a capacity of 100,000 wafers per month, is expected to be completed before 2030.

For logic chips, Terafab is working with Intel and is also in talks with TSMC. It is understood to be developing a separate manufacturing process for memory chips.

A representative from an overseas equipment supplier said, “My understanding is that Musk initially explored acquiring production facilities from Intel, TSMC, and Micron, but shifted toward partnerships after being turned down. I have never seen this level of drive anywhere else in the semiconductor industry.”

A representative from a Korean partner company said, “Even when we send inquiries in the early hours of the morning in the U.S., we get a response within 30 minutes to an hour. Their engineers have decision-making authority, so working with them is completely different from working with typical customers.”

selectedTweets.bestBit: xAI and SpaceX aim for 13 GW AI compute capacity by end of 2027, including 440,000-GPU $NVDA cluster by Q2 2027.
selectedTweets.text:
- Musk announced $ASML and other suppliers have expedited equipment shipments for Terafab, targeting Q3-Q4 2028 volume production.
- Terafab plans first experimental chips at Austin facility in Q2 2027, with primary Texas facility scaling to production within 18 months.
- xAI and SpaceX aim for 13 GW AI compute capacity by end of 2027, including 440,000-GPU $NVDA cluster by Q2 2027.

> $ASML's commitment to expedite EUV equipment shipments validates Terafab's aggressive timeline and signals willingness from critical suppliers to support vertically integrated manufacturing outside traditional ecosystems.
> The 1 TW/year output goal and dual-track facility development (research plus production) represent substantial near-term demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment if timelines hold.
